title: Flat finitely presented relative image from an acyclic section algebra
statement: Let $S$ be any scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $f:Y\to S$ a proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], flat [def-weil-flat-morphism], finitely presented [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] morphism with nonempty geometric fibres of pure dimension one [def-weil-pure-dimension]. Let $M$ be an invertible module [def-sc-invertible-module]. Suppose $f_*\mathcal O_Y=\mathcal O_S$ universally. Suppose, for every $j\geq1$, that $H^i(Y_{\bar s},M_{\bar s}^{\otimes j})=0$ for every geometric point $\bar s$ and every $i>0$, that $A_j=f_*M^{\otimes j}$ is finite locally free (locally a finite direct sum of copies of $\mathcal O_S$), and that its canonical comparison with the direct image on every base change is an isomorphism. Suppose evaluation $f^*A_1\to M$ and all section-multiplication maps $\operatorname{Sym}^j A_1\to A_j$ are surjective, with module pullback as in [def-pc-module-pullback]. On each geometric fibre let $h_{\bar s}:Y_{\bar s}\to\mathbf P(A_1\otimes\kappa(\bar s))$ be the evaluation map. Assume its scheme-theoretic image $Z_{\bar s}$ (the closed subscheme defined by the kernel of the structure-sheaf map to the direct image) satisfies $(h_{\bar s})_*\mathcal O_{Y_{\bar s}}=\mathcal O_{Z_{\bar s}}$ as modules on that projective space, and $R^i(h_{\bar s})_*\mathcal O_{Y_{\bar s}}=0$ for $i>0$. Form $A=\mathcal O_S\oplus\bigoplus_{j\geq1}A_j$ with section multiplication [def-weil-pbc-graded-sheaf-structures]. Then $X=\operatorname{Proj}_S A$ [def-nagata-relative-proj] is flat and finitely presented over $S$, and the quotient $\operatorname{Sym} A_1\to A$ defines a closed immersion $X\hookrightarrow\mathbf P_S(A_1)$ [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism]. Evaluation defines a proper surjective $S$-morphism $q:Y\to X$ with $q^*\mathcal O_X(1)\simeq M$ whose composite with this immersion is the evaluation map. On every geometric fibre this identifies $X_{\bar s}$ with $Z_{\bar s}$ as a closed subscheme and $q_{\bar s}$ with the factor of $h_{\bar s}$ through its scheme-theoretic image. The construction and these comparisons commute with arbitrary base change and with isomorphisms of $(Y/S,M)$.

source.place: Tags 068A (lemma-flat-finite-presentation-perfect) and 0B6G (lemma-perfect-proper-perfect-direct-image); the latter is stated over Noetherian bases and is used after finite-presentation descent. Canonical cohomology base change is perfect.tex Tag 0A1H (lemma-base-change-tensor-perfect). Relative Proj quotient is constructions.tex Tag 01O4 (lemma-apply-relative). Agent-formulated relative-image spreading consequence isolating the arbitrary-base finite-presentation issue in Knudsen Section 2 Proposition 2.1; none of these tags alone states this consequence, and the evaluation morphism is not assumed flat.

proof.text: Work over an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$ on which $A_1$ is free of rank $r$. If $U$ is nonempty then $r>0$: otherwise the surjective evaluation map would be zero on a nonempty geometric fibre. Set $C=\Gamma(U,A)$ and $B=R[x_1,\ldots,x_r]$. The given multiplication surjections give the graded quotient $B\twoheadrightarrow C$. Relative Proj functoriality gives a closed immersion $i:X_U=\operatorname{Proj}C\hookrightarrow P=\mathbf P^{r-1}_U$. The projective-bundle quotient description identifies this with the stated embedding into $\mathbf P_U(A_1)$. In particular $P/U$ and $X_U/U$ are proper, so they are quasi-compact and separated. The standard charts of $P/U$ are polynomial algebras in $r-1$ variables, so $P/U$ is of finite type, as required for the proper-image theorem in step 3. These constructions agree on restrictions to affine refinements of overlaps.

The adjunction evaluations in all degrees form a graded map $f^*A\to\bigoplus_{j\geq0}M^{\otimes j}$; its degree-one part is surjective. The canonical map from the generation locus into relative Proj therefore has generation locus all of $Y$, giving $q:Y\to X$. On each affine base chart the degree-one twist comparison is an isomorphism $q^*\mathcal O_X(1)\simeq M$, carrying every tautological section to its evaluation. The corresponding quotient of $f^*A_1$ is exactly the original evaluation, so the projective-bundle quotient bijection identifies $i q$ with $h$, the evaluation map. Since $X/S$ is separated and $Y/S$ proper, $q$ is proper. The canonical chart comparisons in positive degrees also identify $h^*\mathcal O_P(d)$ with $M^{\otimes d}$ compatibly with multiplication.

source.place: Tag 01O9 (lemma-invertible-map-into-relative-proj); canonical twist comparison; proper-to-separated permanence.

proof.text: Fix a coordinate section $s\in C_1$. The inverse image under $h$ of the standard affine open $D_+(s)$ of $P$ is the nonvanishing open $Y_s$. Apply section localization with $\mathcal F=\mathcal O_Y$. Its degree-zero fractions use only nonnegative powers, whose sections are precisely $C_n$ (including $C_0=R$). Thus $\Gamma(Y_s,\mathcal O_Y)=C_{(s)}$, by the map $a/s^n\mapsto a|_{Y_s}/s^n$. Proj standard-chart sections identify the same map with the unit $\mathcal O_X\to q_*\mathcal O_Y$. Since q is proper, its direct image is quasi-coherent by the cited derived-direct-image theorem. The affine tilde/Gamma equivalence therefore promotes this section isomorphism to a sheaf isomorphism on each chart, hence globally. In particular $h_*\mathcal O_Y=i_*\mathcal O_X$, so $X$ is the scheme-theoretic image of $h$. Apply the proper-image theorem to $Y_U/U$ and the separated finite-type target $P/U$ established in step 1. Its image is exactly the closed subscheme $i(X_U)$, by the computed kernel of $\mathcal O_P\to h_*\mathcal O_Y$, so its proper surjective factor is the already constructed $q$. This calculation uses no vanishing of $H^1(Y,\mathcal O_Y)$.

On the chart just used, $C_{(s)}$ is the sequential colimit $C_0\xrightarrow{s}C_1\xrightarrow{s}C_2\to\cdots$ as an $R$-module: a class of $a\in C_n$ is $a/s^n$, and equality of fractions is exactly equality after multiplication by a further power of $s$. Every $C_n$ is finite projective over $R$ by the affine sections theorem for finite locally free modules; this includes $C_0=R$. Hence each is flat, and their filtered colimit is flat. The affine flatness criterion gives flatness of $X_U\to U$ on every standard chart. Varying $U$ proves $X\to S$ flat.

source.place: Tag 01M7 (lemma-proj-sheaves), homogeneous localization charts; Algebra Tag 05UT (lemma-colimit-flat).

proof.text: For $j\geq1$ put $E_j=Rf_*M^{\otimes j}$. An invertible module is locally free of rank one and finitely presented on $Y$; since $f$ is flat it is flat over $S$. The proper finite-presentation perfect-base-change theorem therefore makes $E_j$ perfect and identifies each geometric derived fibre with $R\Gamma(Y_{\bar s},M_{\bar s}^{\otimes j})$. These fibres are concentrated in degree zero, by the assumed higher-cohomology vanishing, with dimension the rank of $A_j$ by the assumed degree-zero base change. On an open where that rank is $a$, every geometric point belongs to the degree-zero rank-$a$ perfect locus. This locus is open with the universal property in the cited statement, hence is the whole rank open. Thus $E_j\simeq A_j[0]$. Over affine $U$, quasi-coherent cohomology vanishes in positive degrees by applying the affine Cech theorem to the one-member cover. The degenerate Leray comparison now gives $H^p(Y_U,M^{\otimes j})=0$ for every $p>0$ and $j\geq1$.

source.place: Tag 0B91 (lemma-flat-proper-perfect-direct-image-general), (2); the open perfect locus with prescribed degree and rank.

proof.text: Apply cohomology localization to $Y_U$, $M$ and $\mathcal O_{Y_U}$ in every degree $p>0$. Each fraction $\xi/s^n$ can be represented with $n\geq1$ by multiplying numerator and denominator by $s$. Its numerator then lies in $H^p(Y_U,M^{\otimes n})=0$, by the preceding step. Thus $H^p(Y_s,\mathcal O_Y)=0$. Since $h$ is proper, its higher direct images are quasi-coherent by the derived-direct-image theorem. On the affine $D_+(s)\subset P$, the affine Cech theorem and degenerate Leray identify $\Gamma(D_+(s),R^p h_*\mathcal O_Y)$ with this zero group. A quasi-coherent module on an affine scheme is determined by its sections, so $R^p h_*\mathcal O_Y=0$ on the cover, hence globally. Together with step 3 this gives $Rh_*\mathcal O_Y\simeq i_*\mathcal O_X[0]$.

source.place: Tag 09MR (lemma-invert-s-cohomology); affine Leray and quasi-coherence of higher direct images.

proof.text: Let $K=Rh_*\mathcal O_Y$ on $P=\mathbf P^{r-1}_R$. It has quasi-coherent cohomology. For each $d=0,\ldots,r-1$, compose the projection-formula isomorphism $K\otimes^{\mathbf L}\mathcal O_P(d)\simeq Rh_*(M^{\otimes d})$ with the normalized derived global-sections/direct-image comparison. This gives, in $D(R)$, $R\Gamma(P,K\otimes^{\mathbf L}\mathcal O_P(d))\simeq R\Gamma(Y_U,M^{\otimes d})$, and the same comparison for $f_U$ identifies the latter with $R\Gamma(U,E)$, $E=R(f_U)_*M^{\otimes d}$. Proper finite-presentation perfect base change for $Y_U/U$ makes $E$ perfect in $D(\mathcal O_U)$, hence pseudo-coherent; here $d=0$ uses $\mathcal O_Y$, and no degree-zero acyclicity is needed. $E$ has quasi-coherent cohomology, so the affine derived equivalence gives $E\simeq\widetilde{M^\bullet}$ for a complex $M^\bullet$ of $R$-modules representing $R\Gamma(U,E)$. The affine pseudo-coherence criterion then makes $M^\bullet$ quasi-isomorphic to a bounded-above complex of finite free $R$-modules, i.e. $R\Gamma(U,E)$ is pseudo-coherent in $D(R)$. The finite twist test therefore implies that $K$ is pseudo-coherent on $P$. Since step 6 identifies it with $i_*\mathcal O_X[0]$, that single module is pseudo-coherent.

source.place: Tag 0CSG (lemma-pseudo-coherent-on-projective-space), (5) => (1); cohomology.tex Tag 0B54 (lemma-projection-formula-perfect) for the invertible twist, Tag 0B91 (lemma-flat-proper-perfect-direct-image-general), and cohomology.tex Tag 0D5T (derived Leray). Perfect/pseudo-coherent objects on an affine scheme: perfect.tex Tags 06Z0 (lemma-affine-compare-bounded) and 08E7 (lemma-pseudo-coherent-affine).

proof.text: By pseudo-coherence, locally $i_*\mathcal O_X[0]$ has a bounded-above finite-free resolution. Remove its finitely many positive-degree terms from the top down: exactness at the top gives a surjection onto a finite free module, which splits locally, so the resulting remaining top term is finite locally free. Repetition gives a model with top degree zero, hence a finite presentation $\mathcal O^a\to\mathcal O^b\to i_*\mathcal O_X\to0$. Apply the finite-presentation kernel theorem to the surjection $\mathcal O_P\to i_*\mathcal O_X$: its ideal kernel is locally finitely generated. Around each point of $P$, shrink the neighbourhood on which these finitely many ideal generators exist to a distinguished open $D(g)$ of a standard chart $\operatorname{Spec}R[t_1,\ldots,t_{r-1}]$. Quasi-coherence identifies the restricted ideal with the ideal generated by these sections in $R[t_1,\ldots,t_{r-1}]_g$. Thus the inverse image in $X$ is the spectrum of this ring modulo finitely many equations. Explicitly the localized polynomial ring is $R[t_1,\ldots,t_{r-1},u]/(gu-1)$, a finitely presented $R$-algebra. Quotienting by finitely many equations and composing finite presentations gives $X/S$ locally of finite presentation. Its properness from step 1 supplies quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness, so it is finitely presented.

source.place: Tag 08E7 (pseudo-coherent affine finite-free models); Tag 01BP (lemma-kernel-surjection-finite-free-onto-finite-presentation), (1); finite presentations on standard projective charts.

proof.text: For any $T\to S$, the stipulated canonical comparisons $g^*A_j\simeq(f_T)_*M_T^{\otimes j}$, including degree zero, respect multiplication: evaluation of $1\otimes a$ and $1\otimes b$ gives the product $1\otimes ab$. Thus they identify the pulled-back graded algebra with the section algebra on $T$. Arbitrary relative-Proj base change identifies $X_T$ with its Proj, and the canonical generation-locus map is compatible with this base change. The twist comparison carries $a\in A_1$ to its evaluated section on both sides, so agrees after pullback. The quotient into the projective bundle agrees as well, by the quotient bijection. Repeating step 3 over affine opens of $T$ identifies this $X_T$ with the scheme-theoretic image of $h_T$. For $T=\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\bar s)$ this is exactly $Z_{\bar s}$ and identifies $q_{\bar s}$ with the indicated factor. This proves the geometric-fibre comparison without assuming that arbitrary scheme-theoretic images commute with nonflat base change.

source.place: Tags 01O3 (lemma-relative-proj-base-change), 01O9 (canonical generated-line map); the section-localization calculation of step 3.

proof.text: An isomorphism of pairs $(Y/S,M)$ identifies the graded algebras by sending a section to its pullback and using the supplied line-module isomorphism in each tensor power. This respects unit, products and evaluation. Proj functoriality gives the induced isomorphism of $X$; on every standard chart it sends $a/s^n$ to the corresponding fraction. The canonical Proj maps and the twist comparisons are characterized by these evaluated sections, so the resulting squares for $q$, $i$ and $\mathcal O(1)$ commute. The same fraction formulas show that the base-change comparisons compose and are identities for identity changes. Thus all comparisons have the claimed functoriality.
